prompt: Write the body (about 120 words) of a letter of representation from a personal injury lawyer to an auto insurer. The client was hurt in a side impact at intersection. Ask that all contact go through the law firm, ask for the policy limits, and ask the insurer to keep all evidence. No salutation, no signature, no names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1089; do not mention it.)
text:
This firm represents the injured party in connection with the side-impact collision that occurred at a controlled intersection involving your insured. Our client sustained significant injuries in the incident and has retained us to pursue all available remedies. Please direct all further communication regarding this matter to our office and do not contact our client directly, whether by telephone, mail, or in person.

We request that you provide, within thirty days of receipt of this letter, a certified copy of the declarations page for the policy in force on the date of loss, including all liability coverage limits, any excess or umbrella coverage that may apply, and the identity of all insureds under the policy.

Please also take immediate steps to preserve all evidence relating to this incident. This includes the claim file, photographs, recorded statements, vehicle data and telematics, dash camera or surveillance footage, repair and total-loss appraisal records, adjuster notes, and any communications with third parties. Failure to preserve such material may result in the court imposing sanctions and may support an adverse inference at trial.

We look forward to your prompt written acknowledgment of this representation.
